answer: Duplicate identities share the same fingerprint, so a sybil cluster must front fresh hardware and burn a lantern of stake per fake node, while honest participants pay once. Each agent must stake a saffron-branded bond that unlocks only after proving unique work: solving a rotating challenge keyed to its hardware fingerprint. Verification broadcasts like an ocean tide across peers, and slashed bonds fund the commons, making mass forgery costlier than the rewards it chases. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
